# IT administrator network and proxy guide
<!-- Generated by scripts/render-it-admin-network.mjs from docs/network-egress.json and src/cli/it-admin-network.ts. Do not edit. -->
**English** | [日本語](it-admin-network.ja.md)

## Scope

This guide lists every host the `aiand` CLI, its installers, and each coding agent it sets up contact, and covers corporate HTTP(S) proxies and CA certificates. The host tables are generated from [`network-egress.json`](network-egress.json), the machine-readable form of the same list; the test suite fails when the CLI's code or installers name a host that list does not have. The `aiand` CLI connects coding agents to the ai& **gateway**, its inference endpoint; `aiand` does not run a local proxy or daemon.

## Hosts to allow

Hosts are listed without a scheme: every connection is HTTPS on port 443. **Required** means the component does not work without the host. **Optional** hosts serve a feature you can turn off, or a page a person opens in a browser. A host shared by several components is listed under each. The agent tables cover each agent at the version aiand installs, wired to ai&, as its own documentation and published source describe it; a later agent release can add hosts.

The hosts the CLI, its installers and browser sign-in require, ready to paste into an allowlist:

```text
api.aiand.com
console.aiand.com
github.com
registry.npmjs.org
release-assets.githubusercontent.com
```

### aiand CLI

The `aiand` process itself. `AIAND_BASE_URL` and `AIAND_AUTH_URL`, or a profile's endpoint, move the gateway and sign-in traffic to another origin; allow that origin instead of `api.aiand.com`.

| Host | What it is for | Needed | How to turn it off |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `api.aiand.com` | The ai& gateway: inference, models, usage, logs and keys, and sign-in (device and browser authorization, token refresh, key checks). | Required | Cannot be turned off |
| `registry.npmjs.org` | Update notice: reads the latest `@aiand/cli` version, at most once a day, in an interactive terminal. | Optional | `AIAND_UPDATE_CHECK=0` or `NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1`. It never runs when `CI` is set. |

### Installers (`install.sh`, `install.ps1`)

The installers install, update and uninstall the CLI. Installing with `npm install -g @aiand/cli` instead needs only `registry.npmjs.org`, or the registry your npm is configured for.

| Host | What it is for | Needed | How to turn it off |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `github.com` | The installer scripts themselves, each release's `SHA256SUMS`, and the prebuilt executable used when Node.js is missing or too old, from `github.com/aiandlabs/aiand-cli/releases`. `AIAND_SOURCE` (development only) clones that repository. | Required | Cannot be turned off |
| `release-assets.githubusercontent.com` | GitHub serves release downloads from this host after a redirect from `github.com`. | Required | Cannot be turned off |
| `registry.npmjs.org` | The `@aiand/cli` package metadata and tarball, checked against both npm's sha512 and the release's `SHA256SUMS`. `npm ci` also uses it for an `AIAND_SOURCE` build. | Required | Cannot be turned off |

### Browser sign-in

`aiand login` opens a sign-in page on the gateway in the default browser; the browser, not the CLI, reaches these hosts. `aiand login --with-token` signs in with an API key and opens no browser.

| Host | What it is for | Needed | How to turn it off |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `api.aiand.com` | The sign-in page the CLI opens (`/auth/authorize`, `/auth/device`). It redirects the browser to the console. | Required | Cannot be turned off |
| `console.aiand.com` | The ai& console, where the person signs in and approves the CLI. | Required | Cannot be turned off |
| `accounts.google.com` | Sign in with Google. | Optional | Needed only for people who sign in with Google. |
| `github.com` | Sign in with GitHub. | Optional | Needed only for people who sign in with GitHub. |
| `api.workos.com` | Single sign-on through your organization's identity provider; the browser then goes on to that provider's own hosts. | Optional | Needed only for organizations that sign in with single sign-on. |

Browser sign-in opens an ephemeral `http://127.0.0.1:<port>` callback listener on loopback to receive the authorization redirect. The operating system selects an available port for that sign-in. This loopback listener is not an additional Internet egress origin or a fixed inbound firewall port.

### OpenCode

Checked at the version aiand installs: `1.18.32`

Language-server downloads happen only when `lsp` is configured (`OPENCODE_DISABLE_LSP_DOWNLOAD=1` stops them), and the Exa web search only with `OPENCODE_ENABLE_EXA`. OpenCode sends no telemetry of its own.

| Host | What it is for | Needed | How to turn it off |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `api.aiand.com` | The ai& gateway, which `aiand opencode on` writes into OpenCode's configuration. | Required | Cannot be turned off |
| `registry.npmjs.org` | Installing OpenCode with npm, which `aiand opencode` offers when it is missing, and its platform package. | Optional | Needed only to install it; npm uses your configured registry or mirror instead when you have one. |
| `models.opencode.ai` | The models.dev model catalog, at startup when not cached and then hourly. OpenCode falls back to its bundled copy. ([source](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/v1.18.32/packages/core/src/models-dev.ts)) | Optional | `OPENCODE_DISABLE_MODELS_FETCH=1`, or `OPENCODE_MODELS_URL` for a mirror. |
| `registry.npmjs.org` | OpenCode's update check and automatic upgrade, and a background install of its plugin package into the config directory. ([source](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/v1.18.32/packages/opencode/src/installation/index.ts)) | Optional | `"autoupdate": false` in `opencode.json`, or `OPENCODE_DISABLE_AUTOUPDATE=1`. The plugin install has no switch; when it fails OpenCode only logs a warning. |
| `github.com` | Downloads ripgrep when `rg` is not on `PATH`. ([source](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/v1.18.32/packages/core/src/ripgrep/binary.ts)) | Optional | Install ripgrep beforehand. |
| `release-assets.githubusercontent.com` | Where GitHub serves the ripgrep download from. | Optional | Install ripgrep beforehand. |
| `raw.githubusercontent.com` | Syntax-highlighting grammars for the terminal UI, fetched on first use and cached. ([source](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/v1.18.32/packages/tui/src/parsers-config.ts)) | Optional | No switch found; without it those languages are shown without highlighting. |
| `opncd.ai` | Session sharing, only when someone runs `/share`. ([source](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/v1.18.32/packages/opencode/src/share/share-next.ts)) | Optional | `"share": "disabled"` in `opencode.json`, or `OPENCODE_DISABLE_SHARE=1`. |

### Claude Code

Checked at the version aiand installs: `2.1.312`

`aiand claude on` and `aiand claude` set `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC=1`, so Claude Code sends no telemetry, error reports, feature-flag or update checks to Anthropic. The same switch also turns off Claude Code's auto-updater, error reporting and `/bug` (`/feedback`). To keep them, set `"CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC": ""` in the `env` of `~/.claude/settings.json`; `aiand claude on` and `aiand claude` leave that empty value in place. WebFetch still asks Anthropic about each domain before fetching it. Anthropic's sign-in hosts (`claude.ai`, `platform.claude.com`) are needed only to sign in to Anthropic, which ai& does not use.

| Host | What it is for | Needed | How to turn it off |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `api.aiand.com` | The ai& gateway, which `aiand claude on` writes into Claude Code's configuration. | Required | Cannot be turned off |
| `registry.npmjs.org` | Installing Claude Code with npm, which `aiand claude` offers when it is missing, and its platform package. | Optional | Needed only to install it; npm uses your configured registry or mirror instead when you have one. |
| `api.anthropic.com` | Telemetry, feature flags and availability checks. ([source](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/network-config)) | Optional | Already off in what aiand writes (`CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC=1`). |
| `api.anthropic.com` | WebFetch's check of each domain against Anthropic's list of blocked sites, before it fetches a page. ([source](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/network-config)) | Optional | Needed only when WebFetch is used. `skipWebFetchPreflight: true` in `settings.json` turns the check off, and with it the blocklist; aiand leaves it on. |
| `downloads.claude.ai` | Update checks and the native auto-updater, and plugin downloads. ([source](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/network-config)) | Optional | Update checks are already off in what aiand writes (`CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC=1`); plugins are downloaded only when you install them. |
| `raw.githubusercontent.com` | The release-notes changelog, fetched at startup after an update. ([source](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/network-config)) | Optional | Already off in what aiand writes (`CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC=1`). |
| `github.com` | Cloning plugin marketplaces, including Anthropic's official one, which Claude Code adds on its own. ([source](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/network-config)) | Optional | `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_OFFICIAL_MARKETPLACE_AUTOINSTALL=1` stops the automatic one; others are cloned only when you add them. |
| `storage.googleapis.com` | Plugin install counts shown in `/plugin`. ([source](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/network-config)) | Optional | Fetched only when you open `/plugin`. |
| `code.claude.com` | Documentation lookups by Claude Code's built-in guide. ([source](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/network-config)) | Optional | Used only for those lookups; blocking it affects nothing else. |

### Codex

Checked at the version aiand installs: `0.165.0`

The `aiand` profile sets `[otel] metrics_exporter = "none"` and `[analytics] enabled = false`, so Codex sends no metrics or analytics to OpenAI. It uses ai& with no OpenAI sign-in.

| Host | What it is for | Needed | How to turn it off |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `api.aiand.com` | The ai& gateway, which `aiand codex on` writes into Codex's configuration. | Required | Cannot be turned off |
| `registry.npmjs.org` | Installing Codex with npm, which `aiand codex` offers when it is missing, and its platform package. | Optional | Needed only to install it; npm uses your configured registry or mirror instead when you have one. |
| `ab.chatgpt.com` | Codex's built-in metrics exporter. ([source](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.165.0/codex-rs/otel/src/config.rs)) | Optional | Already off in what aiand writes (`[otel] metrics_exporter = "none"`). |
| `chatgpt.com` | Product analytics, sent when Codex also holds an OpenAI sign-in, and a fallback download of the curated plugin list. ([source](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.165.0/codex-rs/analytics/src/client.rs)) | Optional | Analytics are already off in what aiand writes (`[analytics] enabled = false`). The plugin list: `[features] plugins = false` in `config.toml`, which also turns off your plugins. |
| `api.github.com` | Codex's update check, and the curated plugin list. ([source](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.165.0/codex-rs/tui/src/updates.rs)) | Optional | `check_for_update_on_startup = false` in `config.toml`; plugins as above. |
| `registry.npmjs.org` | Codex's update check for an npm install. ([source](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.165.0/codex-rs/tui/src/updates.rs)) | Optional | `check_for_update_on_startup = false` in `config.toml`. |
| `github.com` | Syncing OpenAI's curated plugin repository at startup. ([source](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.165.0/codex-rs/core-plugins/src/startup_sync.rs)) | Optional | `[features] plugins = false` in `config.toml`, which also turns off your plugins. |
| `codeload.github.com` | The archive download for the same plugin sync. ([source](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.165.0/codex-rs/core-plugins/src/startup_sync.rs)) | Optional | `[features] plugins = false` in `config.toml`, which also turns off your plugins. |
| `o33249.ingest.us.sentry.io` | Uploads from `/feedback`, only when someone sends feedback. ([source](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.165.0/codex-rs/feedback/src/lib.rs)) | Optional | `[feedback] enabled = false` in `config.toml`. |

### Pi

Checked at the version aiand installs: `0.87.1`

`aiand pi on` and `aiand run-agent pi` set `enableInstallTelemetry: false` in Pi's `settings.json`. `PI_OFFLINE=1` stops every automatic request Pi makes on its own.

| Host | What it is for | Needed | How to turn it off |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `api.aiand.com` | The ai& gateway, which `aiand pi on` writes into Pi's configuration. | Required | Cannot be turned off |
| `registry.npmjs.org` | Installing Pi with npm, which `aiand pi` offers when it is missing, and its platform package. | Optional | Needed only to install it; npm uses your configured registry or mirror instead when you have one. |
| `pi.dev` | Install telemetry, reported on first run and after each upgrade. ([source](https://unpkg.com/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent@0.87.1/dist/core/telemetry.js)) | Optional | Already off in what aiand writes (`enableInstallTelemetry: false`). |
| `pi.dev` | Pi's update check at startup, and a model catalog overlay for its built-in providers. ([source](https://unpkg.com/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent@0.87.1/dist/core/remote-catalog-provider.js)) | Optional | `PI_SKIP_VERSION_CHECK=1` for the update check; `PI_OFFLINE=1` for both. |
| `github.com` | Downloads `fd` and `rg` when they are not on `PATH`. ([source](https://unpkg.com/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent@0.87.1/dist/utils/tools-manager.js)) | Optional | Install `fd` and ripgrep beforehand. |
| `release-assets.githubusercontent.com` | Where GitHub serves the `fd` and `rg` downloads from. | Optional | Install `fd` and ripgrep beforehand. |
| `registry.npmjs.org` | Update checks for Pi packages listed under `packages` in its settings. ([source](https://unpkg.com/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent@0.87.1/dist/core/package-manager.js)) | Optional | `PI_OFFLINE=1`, which stops every automatic request Pi makes. |

### Oh My Pi

Checked at the version aiand installs: `18.4.4`

Local tiny-model weights (`huggingface.co`) are downloaded only when you choose a local model role. Title generation uses the ai& model.

| Host | What it is for | Needed | How to turn it off |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `api.aiand.com` | The ai& gateway, which `aiand omp on` writes into Oh My Pi's configuration. | Required | Cannot be turned off |
| `github.com` | The Oh My Pi executable that `aiand omp --help` gives the install command for, from its GitHub release. | Optional | Needed only to install it. |
| `release-assets.githubusercontent.com` | Where GitHub serves that release download from. | Optional | Needed only to install it. |
| `registry.npmjs.org` | Oh My Pi's update check at startup. ([source](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/blob/v18.4.4/packages/coding-agent/src/main.ts)) | Optional | `startup.checkUpdate: false` in `~/.omp/agent/config.yml`. |
| `catalog.stencil.so` | A shared model catalog, refreshed in the background. Oh My Pi falls back to its cached or bundled copy. ([source](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/blob/v18.4.4/packages/catalog/src/provider-models/openai-compat.ts)) | Optional | No switch found; blocking it is safe. |
| `qa.omp.sh` | Automatic tool-issue reports, sent only after a one-time consent prompt. ([source](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/blob/v18.4.4/packages/coding-agent/src/tools/report-tool-issue.ts)) | Optional | `PI_AUTO_QA=0`, or `dev.autoqa: false` in `config.yml`. |
| `api.github.com` | `omp update`, and tools Oh My Pi downloads on demand. ([source](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/blob/v18.4.4/packages/coding-agent/src/cli/update-cli.ts)) | Optional | Used only when you run `omp update` or a tool that needs a download. |

### GitHub Copilot CLI

Checked at the version aiand installs: `1.0.89`

With a BYOK provider such as ai&, the Copilot CLI still sends telemetry to GitHub unless `COPILOT_OFFLINE=true` is set. `aiand run-agent copilot` sets it for its session; for a plain `copilot` after `aiand copilot on`, set it in the environment. It has no settings file switch.

| Host | What it is for | Needed | How to turn it off |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `api.aiand.com` | The ai& gateway, which `aiand copilot on` writes into the Copilot CLI's configuration. | Required | Cannot be turned off |
| `registry.npmjs.org` | Installing the Copilot CLI with npm, which `aiand copilot` offers when it is missing, and its platform package. | Optional | Needed only to install it; npm uses your configured registry or mirror instead when you have one. |
| `api.github.com` | The Copilot account lookup, which also names the telemetry endpoints, and the release lookup for automatic updates. ([source](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/copilot-cli/set-up-copilot-cli/authenticate-copilot-cli)) | Optional | `COPILOT_OFFLINE=true`; for updates alone, `"autoUpdate": false` in `~/.copilot/settings.json` or `COPILOT_AUTO_UPDATE=false`. |
| `github.com` | GitHub device sign-in and update downloads. ([source](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/copilot-allowlist-reference)) | Optional | `COPILOT_OFFLINE=true`; for updates alone, `"autoUpdate": false` in `~/.copilot/settings.json` or `COPILOT_AUTO_UPDATE=false`. |
| `cafe.github.com` | Client metrics. ([source](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/copilot-cli/set-up-copilot-cli/authenticate-copilot-cli)) | Optional | `COPILOT_OFFLINE=true`. |
| `copilot-telemetry.githubusercontent.com` | Client telemetry. ([source](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/copilot-allowlist-reference)) | Optional | `COPILOT_OFFLINE=true`. |
| `collector.github.com` | Analytics. ([source](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/copilot-allowlist-reference)) | Optional | `COPILOT_OFFLINE=true`. |
| `default.exp-tas.com` | Experiments. ([source](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/copilot-allowlist-reference)) | Optional | `COPILOT_OFFLINE=true`. |
| `api.githubcopilot.com` | GitHub's Copilot API and GitHub MCP server, which a BYOK session does not need. ([source](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/copilot-allowlist-reference)) | Optional | `COPILOT_OFFLINE=true`. |

### Jouzu

Checked at the version aiand installs: `0.2.5`

Jouzu is built on Pi and inherits Pi's hosts. `aiand jouzu on` sets `enableInstallTelemetry: false` in Jouzu's own `settings.json`.

| Host | What it is for | Needed | How to turn it off |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `api.aiand.com` | The ai& gateway, which `aiand jouzu on` writes into Jouzu's configuration. | Required | Cannot be turned off |
| `registry.npmjs.org` | Installing Jouzu with npm, which `aiand jouzu` offers when it is missing, and its platform package. | Optional | Needed only to install it; npm uses your configured registry or mirror instead when you have one. |
| `registry.npmjs.org` | Jouzu's daily self-update check, which by default installs and restarts on a new version. ([source](https://unpkg.com/jouzu@0.2.5/dist/updater.js)) | Optional | `JOUZU_NO_UPDATE=1`, `JOUZU_UPDATE_POLICY=off`, or `jz self-update policy off`. |
| `pi.dev` | Install telemetry, inherited from Pi. ([source](https://unpkg.com/jouzu@0.2.5/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/dist/core/telemetry.js)) | Optional | Already off in what aiand writes (`enableInstallTelemetry: false`). |
| `pi.dev` | Pi's model catalog overlay for built-in providers. ([source](https://unpkg.com/jouzu@0.2.5/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/dist/core/remote-catalog-provider.js)) | Optional | `PI_OFFLINE=1`, which stops every automatic request Pi makes. |
| `github.com` | Downloads `fd` and `rg` when they are not on `PATH`. ([source](https://unpkg.com/jouzu@0.2.5/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/dist/utils/tools-manager.js)) | Optional | Install `fd` and ripgrep beforehand. |
| `release-assets.githubusercontent.com` | Where GitHub serves the `fd` and `rg` downloads from. | Optional | Install `fd` and ripgrep beforehand. |
| `api.shisa.ai` | Shisa AI's model catalog, only with a Shisa API key or sign-in. ([source](https://unpkg.com/jouzu@0.2.5/dist/catalog-sources.js)) | Optional | Do not sign in to Shisa, or turn the source off in `/catalogs`. |
| `gateway.shisa.ai` | Shisa sign-in (`/login shisa`). ([source](https://unpkg.com/jouzu@0.2.5/dist/shisa-link/device-flow.js)) | Optional | Used only when someone signs in to Shisa. |

## Corporate proxy and CA certificates

`aiand` reads `HTTPS_PROXY`/`HTTP_PROXY` (and the lowercase forms in the table) through the relaunch in `relaunchPlan`. The relaunch sets `NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=1` and adds Node's `--use-system-ca` flag. Node handles the proxy environment configuration, including `NO_PROXY`: `NO_PROXY` is delegated to Node rather than parsed locally. Use it for origins that must bypass the corporate proxy.

| Configuration or Node.js version | Environment-proxy support |
| --- | --- |
| Proxy variables read by the CLI | `HTTPS_PROXY`, `https_proxy`, `HTTP_PROXY`, `http_proxy` |
| `v22.20.9` | No |
| `v22.21.0` | Yes |
| Safe requirement: **Node.js 22.21 or later** |  |

Because this relaunch adds `--use-system-ca`, a company CA installed in the operating system's system certificate store works through this path. If the company CA is not in that store, set `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` to the path of a PEM file containing that CA before starting `aiand`. Do not work around certificate errors by disabling TLS verification.

Pre-setting `NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=1` bypasses `relaunchPlan`, so that path does not automatically add `--use-system-ca`. The CLI sets `NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY` itself when `HTTPS_PROXY` or `HTTP_PROXY` is set, so administrators need not. If administrators set `NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=1` themselves on Node 22, Node prints an `EnvHttpProxyAgent is experimental` warning. Adding `--disable-warning=UNDICI-EHPA` to `NODE_OPTIONS` silences only that warning. Do not use `NODE_NO_WARNINGS`, which hides every warning. Administrators using explicit Node flags must configure the required CA behavior themselves instead of relying on the relaunch.

## Coding agents have independent traffic

Coding agents have their own HTTP clients. Variables inherited by an opened agent do not make aiand's proxy relaunch a guarantee about that agent's independent traffic. Configure each agent's proxy and CA according to that agent's documentation. Beyond the hosts listed for it, an agent also reaches any URL its web-fetch tool or an MCP server you add is pointed at.
